transcript:
Meeting Header
Date: 2025-05-07
Start: 10:00 AM PDT
Duration: ~45 mins
Attendees: Alex Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Liu (Redwood SE), Jason Lee (CTO, Arcadia), Maya Rodriguez (Lead ML Eng), Tom Nguyen (Infra), Sofia Alvarez (Security)
Shared: pilot-runbook.md (link), network-diagram.png (link), security-summary.pdf (link)

Summary:
Quick weekly sync on the Redwood Private VPC pilot; reviewed last week's benchmark (baseline latency/cost), discussed routing/hairpinning issues, plan for control plane upgrade, and next steps for deep packet capture window.

Topics:
- Benchmarks: 95th/99th tail latency improvements after KV cache tuning
- Networking: VPC peering asymmetry, NACLs, and cross-account route propagation
- Upgrades: private control plane minor version bump and canary plan
- Security: KMS integration questions and audit logging retention

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining, we've got 45 minutes, we'll do a quick status, then dig into the network findings and the upgrade plan, then capture next steps
[00:12] Jason: cool yeah thanks Alex, we got some ops people on the line too so we can action things quickly
[00:20] Priya: quick note, i ran the prefix cache tweak you asked about last week, it's live on the pilot nodes as of yesterday, so numbers in the dashboard reflect that
[00:28] Maya: ok great, i saw some improvement in the p95s but p99 still spikes during the mid-day traffic window, about 1.1 to 1.3 seconds, baseline was 1.8 so better but still higher than we need
[00:43] Jordan: right, the p99 spike looks correlated with reauth requests hitting the control plane, there was an observed 30-60s window where token refreshes pile up, causes KV cache misses
[00:58] Tom: we pulled the VPC flow logs, looks like there are a handful of flows being routed out to the transit gateway and back in, hairpinning maybe? i'm attaching the short capture to the notes
[01:12] Priya: yeah that's the asymmetry I mentioned earlier - cross-account peering + TGW route propagation created a path that adds an extra hop and increases RTT, so cold KV cache misses + extra hop = the p99 tail
[01:30] Maya: makes sense, we also saw a few 502s during the peak window; not many but enough to affect our SLA target. not sure if those are from the control plane or from node oom kills
[01:44] Jordan: logs show one node rebooted due to a kernel OOM around 10:42 UTC, likely unrelated to network but we should scope resource limits on the pilot nodes, increase oom_score_adj or tune the cgroup memory limits
[01:58] Jason: on the security side, Sofia had a question about KMS integration - can the control plane call our customer-managed KMS or does it require passing keys to Redwood?
[02:12] Sofia: yes, we need to understand key policies, audit logs, and whether HSM is used. regulatory team flagged this as a gating item for prod
[02:24] Alex: short answer, pilot supports customer-managed KMS via cross-account roles, we maintain no plaintext keys, but i'll have Priya and security docs to show the exact policy bindings, we'll share the SOC2 excerpt and KMS integration notes after this call
[02:38] Priya: noted, i'll attach the policy sample and the key rotation cadence. also we recommended using envelope encryption to minimize token exposure in logs
[02:52] Maya: thanks - that will help our compliance review. back on performance - could we try a model variant with a smaller KV memory profile to see if cache pressure drops?
[03:05] Jordan: yes we can push a quantized variant; it reduces memory footprint and the KV cache working set, should lower cold-miss latency but might slightly increase per-token compute time. tradeoff discussion: latency tail vs cost and accuracy
[03:26] Jason: our main SLO is 95% < 300ms, 99% < 800ms. We're not hitting that yet. Clarifying: this is for API calls used in patient triage workflows, so it's strict
[03:40] Alex: understood. given that, immediate actions are: 1) fix the routing/hairpin issue 2) run e2e bench with quantized variant 3) scope control plane upgrade canary to reduce reauth pileup
[03:55] Tom: i can make the routing change but we need a maintenance window, when were you thinking?
[04:02] Priya: would prefer Tues night 01:00-03:00 UTC to do a packet capture during a normal load window; we can schedule rollback if we see regressions
[04:14] Jason: ok that works. Tom will open the window and give Redwood access for tshark capture
[04:24] Sofia: a quick security note: if Redwood needs to perform packet capture, can it be limited to the subnet-level mirror and delivered to our S3 with encryption? we don't want broad access to PII flows
[04:38] Alex: yes we'll use VPC traffic mirroring to your capture bucket with SSE-KMS - Redwood won't retain copies. we'll also redact any payloads in our diagnostic tooling. i'll put the exact capture policy in the runbook
[04:54] Maya: thanks. one more infra item - can we bump the node instance types in the pilot from r5.large to r5.xlarge to eliminate OOM candidates? that's low effort and likely to reduce reboots
[05:06] Jordan: that should help, but note cost goes up; for the pilot we recommend a temporary bump and measure memory pressure across 48 hours before changing autoscaling policies
[05:18] Jason: acceptable, pilot budget allows it for now. please document the cost delta in the benchmark report
[05:26] Priya: will do. also ran a quick test of batching settings; with continuous batching set to 20ms we saw slightly higher throughput but it bumped p95 by ~30ms - i'll include both configs in the report
[05:42] Maya: cool. question about the control plane upgrade - what's in the minor release and how risky is a canary?
[05:52] Alex: minor release includes smarter token refresh backoff and a fix for reauth storming; risk is low but we still want a canary (5% of traffic) measured over 24h. if we see increase in 5xxs or p99 we rollback automatically
[06:08] Jordan: our suggested canary plan: 5% allocation to canary, collect 95/99 latencies, error rates, and control plane CPU/memory metrics; automatic rollback if p99 increases by >15% or 5xxs doubles
[06:23] Jason: sounds reasonable. can you share the exact rollback thresholds and the instrumentation dashboard?
[06:30] Alex: yes i'll share the canary runbook and Grafana link after the call
[06:36] Tom: i uploaded the route table snapshots and a short pcap to the shared folder (link in notes)
[06:42] Priya: thanks, i'll correlate that with the pilot node logs. also, we've noticed a couple of mis-attributed speaker lines in the automatic transcription, so some names in the transcript may be wrong - apologies, that's fireflies quirks
[06:56] Maya: ha, yeah we've seen that before. final question: if the canary looks good, what is the lead time to push to all pilot nodes and then prod?
[07:07] Jordan: can push to all pilot nodes within 48 hours after canary clear, prod depends on your approvals but typically 7-14 days for scheduling and compliance checks
[07:20] Jason: that's fine. will team prioritize security review in parallel.
[07:28] Alex: ok recapping next steps - Priya runs e2e bench and shares results; Tom schedules packet capture window and gives access; Redwood shares runbook, canary thresholds, and KMS policy; Sofia to confirm audit gating. we'll reconvene same time next week unless we need an earlier blocker call
[07:48] Jason: perfect thanks everyone
[07:52] Alex: thanks all, talk soon

End of transcript
